newsitem.title: UK: Investors to hesitate until DMG sorted out.
newsitem.headline: Investors to hesitate until DMG sorted out.

text.p: The suspension of three Deutsche Morgan Grenfell investment funds will make investors hesitate but the firm's longer-term reputation remains safe for now, industry analysts said on Tuesday.
Deutsche Bank's London-based investment banking arm suspended dealings in the funds, totalling nearly 1.4 billion pounds ($2.2 billion), on Monday while it looks into "possible irregularities".
In a business where a firm's "name" is crucial, it could face a rocky patch. Analysts said DMG was likely to move quickly to quell any speculation and return the funds to an even keel.
"Fund management, in common with investment banking, is a business that depends on reputation," said one analyst who declined to be named.
"They will probably not see an outflow of funds but you will probably find some investors holding back from putting in any new money."
Analysts said it was far too early to be looking at more serious implications, such as changing earnings forecasts for the parent bank.
On Monday, Britain's investment management regulator IMRO said it was working closely with DMG following the suspension by the bank of Peter Young who managed two of the funds.
DMG said it would face up to its responsibilities if shareholders had lost out.

"Coming so soon after the Jardine Fleming case, the Morgan Grenfell situation is bound to have an effect on investors but doesn't look to us as though the two cases have anything much in common," said another banking analyst.

Last week, IMRO fined Jardine Fleming Asset Management, a joint venture between Jardine Matheson and British investment bank Robert Fleming, 700,000 pounds after an investigation which exposed flagrant flouting of trading rules.
"It looks like a coincidence," said one analyst, "and I don't think you can make any judgments about the industry generally from these cases."
DMG has maintained a high profile over the last year after Deutsche, which bought Morgan Grenfell in 1989, decided to make it the basis of its investment banking activities.
It has been relatively aggressive in recruiting staff, notably from the former SG Warburg, and was sued by rival ING Barings after it took Barings' Latin American equities team.
The two firms later came to an agreement which stopped the action reaching the courts.

Embarrassment at Morgan Grenfell, which has around 70 billion pounds under management, is increased by the fact that it is bidding to take on the 500 million pounds Kleinwort European Privatisation Fund (KEPIT).
Analysts said the outcome of the investigation would be crucial.
"I can't see that DMG could continue with its interest in KEPIT if they are seen to have done wrong," said one analyst. "They would have to have a lot of front to do that." ($1=.6406 Pound)
